title: Parabolic Type of a Finite Reductive Group Representation
body_html:
Parabolic Type of a Finite Reductive Group Representation

Let \(G\) be a connected reductive algebraic group over a finite field \(k\), and write \(G(k)\) for its finite group of \(k\)-points.

A horocyclic subgroup of \(G\) is the unipotent radical of a \(k\)-parabolic subgroup. A finite-dimensional representation \(\gamma\) of \(G(k)\) is cuspidal if its average over every nontrivial \(k\)-horocyclic subgroup is zero.

If \(P\) is a \(k\)-parabolic subgroup with unipotent radical \(U\), a representation of \(P(k)\) is cuspidal if \(U(k)\) acts trivially and the induced representation of \(P(k)/U(k)\) is cuspidal.

An irreducible representation \(\gamma\) of \(G(k)\) has the type of \(P\) if \(\gamma|_{P(k)}\) contains a cuspidal representation of \(P(k)\). This type is recorded as the corresponding subset of the Dynkin graph.
